Commentary.Commentary: We are back for Nepal's replay with the bat. The umpires and players are out in the middle. Sana Praveen and Sabitri Dhami are the openers for Nepal Women Under-19. Suabika has the new ball and will start the proceedings. Away we go.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, with only 46 runs to chase, Nepal will step out brimming with confidence and eager to wrap up the game with ease. A strong start will be key to avoiding any unexpected hiccups along the way. On the other hand, Malaysia, despite the daunting challenge, have shown promise with the ball throughout this campaign and will need to deliver their absolute best to pull off a miraculous turnaround with their backs against the wall. The chase begins in just a few minutes so stay tuned!

Riya Sharma is in for a quick chat. She says that their plan was to deliver as many dot balls as they can to create pressure on the batters. She adds that there was not much pressure as compared to their match against Australia Women Under-19. Ends by saying they will chase this with ten wickets in hand and also believes that the openers will do better this time.

Nepal Women Under-19 maintained their stranglehold by striking at regular intervals, never allowing any batter to settle or build momentum. Puja Mahato and Rachana Chaudhary were the standout performers, claiming 4 and 3 wickets respectively, while the rest of the bowling unit provided excellent support to dismantle Malaysia’s lineup efficiently.

Electing to field first, Nepal made an immediate impact as their skipper Puja Mahato led from the front with early breakthroughs, piling the pressure on Malaysia. Aggressive field placements, with no fielders outside the inner circle, choked the flow of runs and made it incredibly difficult for Malaysian batters, who have struggled to find the boundary throughout the tournament, to pierce the gaps.

A clinical performance from Nepal Women Under-19 sees them bundle Malaysia Women Under-19 out for just 45 runs in under 17 overs. Their precision in bowling, combined with outstanding fielding efforts, kept Malaysia under relentless pressure throughout the innings. While the hosts yet again face a batting collapse, Nepal head into the break firmly in control of the game.

Commentary.Commentary: Well then, done with the pre-match formalities and it is now time for the action to begin! The umpires and players are already out in the middle. Final words being spoken by the coach in the Malaysian team huddle before the batters come out. Nepal Women Under-19 now stride out and spread to their fielding positions. Out walk the opening pair of Nur Aliya and Nuni for Malaysia Women Under-19. Puja Mahato, the skipper has the new ball and will kickoff the proceedings for Nepal. Here we go...
Out come the match officials and both teams for the national anthems. It will be the national anthem of Nepal first followed by that of Malaysia.

PITCH REPORT - Marina Iqbal is down in the middle for the pitch analysis. She says the skies are clear and there seems no rain on the radar as of now. Adds that the boundaries are 55 meters throughout and the surface is getting lighter in colour which indicates that it is drying up. Mentions that there is a lot of purchase in it for the bowlers but the batters will have value for their shots as well.

Nur Dania Syuhada, the skipper of Malaysia Women Under-19 says they would have batted first had they won the toss. Adds that it has been a great experience and they are glad to have an opportunity in this World Cup. Concludes that they have one change in their side.

Puja Mahato, the skipper of Nepal Women Under-19 says the overhead conditions and slow outfield is the reason the want to bowl first. Mentions that they tried their best and they want to try and finish the tournament with a win. Concludes that they have a couple of changes in the side.
Malaysia Women Under-19 (Playing XI) - Nuni, Nur Aliya (WK), Husna, Nur Dania Syuhada (C), Suabika, Nuriman, Nur Izzatul Syafiqa, Ain, Batrisyia (in for Adani), Nazwah, Marsya.

Nepal Women Under-19 (Playing XI) - Sana Praveen, Sabitri Dhami, Puja Mahato (C), Jyotsnika Marasini, Seemana KC, Alisha Yadav (WK), Kusum Godar (in for Tirsana Bishwokarma), Krishma Gurung, Rachana Chaudhary, Riya Sharma, Sneha Mahara (in for Anu Kadayat).
TOSS - Nepal Women Under-19 win the coin flip and elect to BOWL first.

Hello and a warm welcome to the second match of the 4th Place Playoff in the 2025 ICC Women's Under-19 T20 World Cup! The bottom-placed teams from Group A and Group D face off as Malaysia Women Under-19 take on Nepal Women Under-19 at the Johor Cricket Academy Oval. Both sides will be eager to conclude their campaign on a high note with a morale-boosting victory.
... MATCH DAY ...

Match 2 of the positional playoffs at the 2025 ICC Women's Under-19 T20 World Cup brings together the fourth-placed teams from Groups A and D at the Johor Cricket Academy Oval. Malaysia Women Under-19, from Group A, face off against Nepal Women Under-19 from Group D as both teams look to finish their maiden Women's Under-19 T20 World Cup campaigns on a positive note. There are plenty of similarities between the two teams, who have both had moments of brilliance with the ball across their three group-stage games. However, batting has been a constant challenge for both, although their fielding has been one of the highlights to go with their bowling. Nepal, in their previous game against Australia, managed to put the opposition under early pressure, supported by excellent fielding. Skipper Puja Mahato has led from the front in the pace department, while Seemana KC has impressed with her off-spin, providing crucial breakthroughs when needed. Nepal’s batting showed some improvement in the game against a formidable Aussie attack, as they managed to bat out the full 20 overs. Puja Mahato has fought a lone fight with the bat, but for Nepal to post or chase a competitive total, she will need more support from the rest of the lineup. As for Malaysia, they faced the West Indies in their last group stage match, which was a must-win for them to progress to the Super Six stage. They showcased commendable resilience with the ball in the first 10 overs but faltered in the next 10, something they will want to tighten up and keep the pressure on for longer periods. With the bat, Malaysia showed improvement with every game in the group stage. They posted their highest total of the tournament in the last outing against the West Indies, and this boost in confidence will certainly be valuable as they look to build on that momentum. Husna and captain Nur Dania Syuhada showed promise during their brief stays, and the duo will be key to Malaysia's batting fortunes as they aim to finish their campaign on a high. With both sides having faced challenges in the group stage, they will be determined to give their best performance and sign off with a much-needed victory. Who will come out on top? We shall find out.
